# Campus Library Reservation System  
## Assignment 2 — Architecture and Quality Plan

## 1. Context and scope

The Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS) will replace the existing study-room reservation tool across three university libraries. Students and staff will search rooms and equipment, create or change reservations, cancel reservations, and receive reminders. Library staff will manage rooms, opening hours, block bookings and utilisation reports. A kiosk outside each room will display the current and next reservation.

CLRS must integrate with three existing systems:

- The university identity provider through SAML;
- Facilities calendars through iCal feeds;
- A read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database.

The main quality constraints are 99.5% monthly availability during opening hours, graceful kiosk operation when offline, availability-search p95 latency below 400 ms with 2,000 concurrent users, authenticated and audited actions, configuration-only onboarding of new campuses, database- and network-independent testing of reservation rules, and deployment or rollback by a two-person team within ten minutes.

This design selects a **hexagonal architecture implemented as a modular monolith**. The domain and application logic are isolated from infrastructure through ports and adapters. A single deployable application and database reduce operational complexity, while explicit boundaries preserve testability
